title: latency-saturation-echo-log-jun24-2026
body:
Attendees: Aisha P., Marco C., Lina R., Samir K., (ops: T. Nguyen async)

Purpose: capture the weekday performance sync focused on a recurring latency saturation signal seen during mixed short/long sequence shadow runs. This is a working capture — notes, hypotheses, and the immediate next steps.

Summary of the symptom:
- Intermittent P99 spikes (~ 1.8–2.6s) during sustained shadow load at 180 QPS despite stable P50/P90. Spikes coincide with burst of short requests (seq<=32) followed by long requests (seq>=512).
- Throughput stays within expected band, but tail latency increases by 2–4x for ~10–30s windows. No obvious GPU saturation (util 55–70%) and no obvious OOM.

Environment for the day’s runs:
- Model: redwood-13b-opt-v2 (FP16)
- Hardware: A100-80GB nodes, driver nv-525, cuda 12.1
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@main (PR 812 kernels), kernel_variant=fast-attn-v3
- Orchestrator: k8s v1.27, nodepool with 4 pods (autoscale disabled for controlled test)
- Config: batch_size_target=48, concurrency_limit=64, kv_cache_mode=on (prefix shared across warm sessions), prefetch=enabled

Test matrix executed (2026-06-24 09:15–13:00):
1) Mixed steady: 60% seq32, 40% seq512, QPS ramp 20->180 (15m steady) — baseline capture
2) Short-burst injection: add 30s spikes of 300 short seqs every 5m — reproduce short->long transition
3) KV cache shadow off vs on: toggle to observe interaction with hot-prefix reuse
4) Kernel A/B: fast-attn-v2 vs fast-attn-v3 (PR 812)
5) Concurrency sweep: concurrency_limit 16/32/64 with batch target fixed

Representative numbers (steady windows, median of 5 samples):
- Baseline (kv_cache=on, kernel=v3, conc=64): P50=42ms, P90=150ms, P99=1.9s (spiky windows)
- Baseline (kv_cache=off): P50=55ms, P90=180ms, P99=420ms (much lower tail)
- Kernel v2 vs v3 (kv_cache=on): v3 P50 8–12% better than v2, but v3 shows higher P99 sensitivity under mixed bursts
- Concurrency 16: P99 drops to ~520ms but total throughput limited to ~110 QPS (backpressure observed)

Observations and immediate interpretations:
- The kv_cache path improves median latency and throughput for steady long sequences but appears to amplify tail latency when short-request bursts cause lots of small cache invalidations/evictions.
- Kernel v3 introduced an optimization in attention scatter that lowers steady latency but may introduce a path that blocks on a small critical section when many short requests interleave with long ones (suspected lock contention or scheduling stall).
- Lowering concurrency reduces tail but at large cost to throughput — classic latency/throughput tradeoff.
- Resource metrics (GPU SM, memory, PCIe) do not show throttling; CPU for the runtime thread pool shows brief spikes aligning with P99 windows.

Hypotheses to test next:
- H1: KV cache eviction thrash on mixed prefixes leads to scheduler spikes — test with larger per-pod kv-cache capacity and different eviction policy.
- H2: Kernel v3 critical section (attention scatter) has lock contention under many tiny tensors — reproduce with microbench that simulates alternating short/long seq paths.
- H3: Orchestrator scheduling (k8s pod-level CPU steal) amplifies rare scheduler pauses — run pinned CPU cores and isolated nodepool.

Planned experiments (next 48h):
- Experiment A: Increase kv_cache capacity 2x, set eviction_policy=LRU-plus and re-run mixed steady. Owner: Marco (ETA 24h).
- Experiment B: Run kernel A/B microbench synthetic harness to measure lock hold times and contention metrics (Lina + Samir, ETA 48h).
- Experiment C: Re-run critical run on dedicated node with CPU pinning and isolated system daemons disabled (Aisha, ETA 36h).
- Experiment D: Shadow run with concurrency limiter that dynamically throttles short-request rate (prototype in PR 826, Samir).

Immediate action items from meeting:
- Marco: spin kv-cache tuning branch and push results to INFR-1749 comment by EOD tomorrow.
- Lina: add microbench harness to repo under benchmarking/micro and open PR referencing this doc.
- Samir: prototype a lightweight admission control heuristic for short requests (sequence-length based) and measure effect on P99.
- Aisha: create a short confluence page with reproducible steps and attach collection of traces (trace ids listed below).

Relevant traces and captures (sample ids):
- trace: shadow-run-20260624-0918 (baseline)
- trace: shortburst-20260624-1045 (injection reproducer)
- perfdump: node-03-20260624-1105 (cpu/gpu timeline)

Notes / open questions to discuss next sync:
- If kv-cache tuning reduces tail, is there secondary cost in increased cold-start latencies for rare prefixes?
- Should we expose an opt-in per-customer toggle for kv-cache strictness? (product question)
- If kernel v3 is root cause, do we consider rolling back or adding a safety gate for mixed-workload pods?

Quick links:
- Related jira: INFR-1749 (root problem capture)
- PR with kernel changes: github PR 812

Summary: we have a reproducible mixed-workload tail-latency spike that correlates with kv-cache usage and the newly introduced kernel v3 fast-attn path. Short-term mitigations (kv cache tuning, concurrency throttles) reduce P99 but impact throughput. Next 48h experiments will aim to isolate which subsystem is dominant (kv cache eviction vs kernel contention vs OS scheduling).

-- Aisha P.
